title: What at-least-once actually promises

prereqs.why: The question is exactly what each guarantee does and does not promise.
The reason at-least-once is workable at all is that duplicates can be made harmless.

statement:
A message queue is configured for **at-least-once** delivery. Consumers pull a message, process it, and then acknowledge it; an unacknowledged message is redelivered after a visibility timeout.

**Which of the following are true?** Select all that apply.
hints: Work through the failure: a consumer finishes the work and then its machine dies before the acknowledgement is sent. What does the broker see, and what does it do?
For the claim about exactly-once, ask what deduplicating at the broker protects against and what it does not. Which end performs the side effect?
At-most-once is the mirror image. If you move the acknowledgement to *before* the processing, which problem goes away and which appears?

options: A consumer may process the same message more than once, so the processing must be idempotent for the system to be correct.
If a consumer crashes after finishing the work but before acknowledging, the message will be delivered again to some consumer.
Genuine exactly-once semantics can be obtained simply by having the broker discard any message whose id it has already delivered.
At-most-once delivery avoids duplicates by acknowledging before processing, at the cost of losing messages when a consumer crashes mid-work.
